plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/24201
NEEDS YOUR CALL: the nine Michigan systems are separate, unnamed utilities, coded here as one aggregate record because none is identified. Delete this record if you prefer not to count unnamed aggregates.
Part of the coordinated July 26-28, 2026 attacks on internet-exposed operational technology at US water and wastewater systems (30+ systems in Minnesota plus Georgia, Michigan, New Jersey and other states; the FBI says at least seven states). CISA's July 30 alert and its July 2026 update describe Iranian-affiliated actors targeting internet-facing PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens), changing passwords and IP addresses to lock operators out and, for the first time, stealing PLC project files. No federal or state attribution has been made; experts suspect Iran's IRGC (pattern consistent with CyberAv3ngers per Tenable), so the actor is coded external Unknown with motive Unknown, and the suspicion is only noted. Method at this specific utility is not public, so hacking variety and vector are Unknown (the campaign generally used internet-exposed devices with default or weak credentials). Template Hacking-ext-unknown used for actor/action only; no data theft was reported, so no confidentiality block, and the asset is the control system with role OT rather than a web application. Consider linking all the July 2026 water records with one campaign_id.
Impact: EGLE says all affected systems kept operating safely with no known public health impact, so no availability impact was coded; integrity Unknown (the 'hostile cyber activity' is not described).
Discovery: not described, so Unknown. Timeline July 2026 (FBI: attacks since July 27). dbir_year 2027.
Victim: unnamed; NAICS 221310 from the issue; government status and size unknown.

event_chain.summary: Hostile activity against water system OT (details not disclosed)

summary: Michigan's Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy said nine Michigan water systems reported hostile cyber activity matching the late-July 2026 attacks on Minnesota water utilities. The state said all affected systems continued to operate safely with no known impacts to public health, and it did not name the systems. The activity was part of the coordinated attacks on internet-exposed water-sector operational technology reported in at least seven states since July 27, 2026.
